aid.value: WashU meets its calculated full demonstrated need for admitted undergraduates. International applicants must request aid during admission; students who initially decline aid cannot apply after the admission decision or during their four years.

attributes.aidShort: Full demonstrated need; request aid with admission

testing.value: The Fall 2027 international first-year checklist makes SAT/ACT optional. Applicants may alternatively submit specified national, IB, A-level or AP results. English proficiency is a separate requirement.

evidence.quote: Optional – Self-reported or official SAT or ACT scores.

english.value: International applicants whose first language is not English must provide official TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test results. Review the linked English-testing requirements for individual circumstances; optional SAT/ACT does not remove this requirement.

fee.value: The non-refundable application fee is $75. WashU waives it for financial-aid applicants and applicants for whom payment would create financial hardship; follow its waiver instructions.

deadline.value: Fall 2027: EA/ED I applications November 2, 2026; ED II/RD January 4, 2027. Aid: EA/ED I November 17; ED II January 11; RD February 1. Signature Scholar priority: December 16, 2026. School-document deadlines differ.

aid.value: Foreign nationals cannot receive Wake Forest need-based aid. International first-year applicants may compete for most merit scholarships, including several full-cost awards. These are highly selective; otherwise applicants must document sufficient funding. International transfers are ineligible for assistance.

attributes.aidShort: Competitive merit awards; no international need-based aid

evidence.quote: need-based financial aid to foreign national students

testing.value: Wake Forest does not require SAT/ACT for international undergraduate admission. Scores become required for consideration only if the applicant elects to have them reviewed; enrolled score-submitters must later provide official results.

evidence.quote: does not require applicants to submit

english.value: English proof is required for non-native speakers or students outside English-medium schooling, using TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo. The international FAQ provides a waiver after at least three years in English-medium schooling. English-test scores are not superscored.

fee.value: The application fee is $85. Applicants who need assistance can request a fee waiver in the indicated application section; the international admissions page explicitly offers this option.

deadline.value: The current first-year page linked to Class of 2031 lists ED I and first-generation Early Action on November 15; ED II and Regular Decision on January 1. Apply by November 15 for most merit scholarships. Foreign-national need-based aid is unavailable.

evidence.quote: Merit-Based Scholarship Deadline to apply: November 15

aid.value: Richmond is need-aware for international applicants and meets calculated full need when all required aid documents arrive on time. Submit Certification of Financial Responsibility and 2027–28 CSS Profile. Aid deadlines: EA/ED I November 15, 2026; ED II/RD February 1, 2027. Late applications lose aid eligibility or receive reduced grants. Awards cover up to eight regular semesters, excluding summer.

attributes.aidShort: Need-aware; full demonstrated need with timely documents

evidence.quote: committed to meeting the full demonstrated financial need of all admitted domestic and international applicants

testing.value: Fall 2027 applicants may apply without SAT/ACT. If scores are selected for review, they must arrive by the credential deadline. Richmond superscores; enrolled score-submitters must provide official results before the fall term.

evidence.quote: applicants may apply with or without standardized test scores

english.value: Non-native English speakers need official TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo results or an approved waiver. Waivers include four years of rigorous English-medium secondary schooling, specified SAT/ACT scores or qualifying AP/IB/A-level English grades. Published competitive scores are not minimum admission cutoffs. Waivers are confirmed after application review; optional interviews do not replace English proof.

evidence.quote: they are not minimum admission scores

fee.value: Richmond offers an application-fee waiver to international students and other applicants living abroad. Follow the Richmond Awarded Fee Waiver instructions linked from its international admissions page. This admission waiver is separate from the CSS Profile waiver process.

evidence.quote: waive the application fee for international students and other applicants living abroad

deadline.value: For the 2026–27 application cycle: ED I/EA applications November 1; ED II/RD January 1. Credential deadlines: ED I November 15, EA December 1, ED II January 15, RD February 15. Apply by December 1 for Richmond Scholars. Financial-aid deadlines are listed separately under aid.
